solves: Shows a short balloon of complementary information, an explanation or context data attached to an element that receives focus, opened at once on keyboard focus and after a short wait on hover, without moving focus to the balloon. On an icon-only button the balloon text is the accessible name of the action.
use_when: To give the action name to every icon-only button.
For complementary information or context data of any element.
For one sentence the person reads at once, before filling in.
do_not_use_when: To put an action, a link or a field inside the balloon: use nph-popover.
To repeat in the balloon the help text of the field: that belongs to nph-field.
To put in the balloon information without which the element cannot be used.
To cut the text with an ellipsis or let it pass two lines: rewrite until it fits.
On a disabled element or on text that does not receive focus: it gets no balloon.
To name an ambiguous action with an icon-only button: on touch the balloon does not open; use a button with text.

text.constraint: The balloon content, already localized by the consuming application, with no action and no link. Empty or whitespace-only shows nothing. The balloon follows the text up to layout/max-tooltip-width and wraps; it fits at most two lines and the text must fit whole, with no ellipsis and no broken word.

for.constraint: The id of the element that opens the balloon, looked up in the same root as the tooltip, like the native label. The element must receive focus: a disabled element gets no balloon, and an element that does not receive focus gets none and emits console.error in development. The tooltip listens on that element and adds its own id to the aria-describedby of the element, or to its aria-labelledby with relation name, keeping what is there and following a change of its own id. Without it, or with an id that matches no element, the balloon is not drawn and console.error is emitted in development.

side.constraint: The preferred side: top, bottom, left or right. The balloon flips to the opposite side when it does not fit, and never leaves the window. It is behavior, not appearance: the Figma component has no side property. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

open.constraint: The state of the balloon. The tooltip turns it on and off by itself, on hover, on keyboard focus, on leave, on blur and on Esc. The consumer may turn it on to show the balloon open, and the same closing rules apply; on an element without focus nothing is drawn.

relation.constraint: What the balloon is to the element: description, the default, added to its aria-describedby, or name, added to its aria-labelledby, for the icon-only button, whose action name is the balloon text, announced once. name needs text. Any other value draws nothing, writes no reference and emits console.error in development.

closed.changes_for_user: The balloon is not shown. The element is still described, or named, by its text.

open.changes_for_user: The balloon is shown next to the element, at space/inline, entering on motion/enter-duration.

business_rules: Keyboard focus on the element opens the balloon at once. A mouse or a pen opens it after resting motion/hover-delay on the element; leaving before the wait ends opens nothing. It never opens on touch.
Click, Enter and Space run the action of the element: they neither open nor close the balloon. A click during the wait cancels it.
The balloon goes only on an element that receives focus. A disabled element and loose text get no balloon: without focus, a keyboard user never sees it.
On an icon-only button the balloon text is the accessible name of the action, announced once (relation name). On any other element it complements the accessible name and does not replace it.
It closes when the pointer leaves the element and the balloon, on blur and with Esc. While the pointer is over the balloon it stays open.

It sits on top by default, flips to the opposite side when it does not fit, and may also sit bottom, left or right. While the element is outside the window the balloon is not drawn; it returns with the element.
It leaves on motion/exit-duration; coming back into the element or the balloon during the exit cancels the closing.
The balloon never takes focus: focus stays on the element that opened it.
The text fits entirely in up to two lines, without ellipsis, automatic hyphenation or broken words.
ai_hints: Use nph-tooltip with relation name to name an icon-only button, or with the default description to give complementary context to an element that receives focus.
Point it at the element with for, which is the id of the element in the same root; the tooltip does the rest.
Do not attach it to a disabled element or to loose text: without focus it gets no balloon.
Do not open it from code to explain a field: it opens by itself on hover after a short wait and on focus at once, and never on touch.
Do not put the help text, the error message or essential information in the balloon: they belong to nph-field or to the element.
Do not add a title, icon, action, link, arrow or border; for content that asks for focus or action, choose nph-popover.
Choose the side only when the default does not suit; the balloon flips by itself when it does not fit.

accessibility.semantics: The host is a role=tooltip from mount, open or closed, with aria-label mirroring the text so the element is described, or named, before the balloon opens. The element points to it with aria-describedby, or with aria-labelledby under relation name.
accessibility.accessible_name: On an icon-only button the balloon text is the accessible name of the action, announced once, through aria-labelledby (relation name). On any other element the balloon complements the accessible name and does not replace it. On touch the icon-only button has no visible name, an accepted exception: the name lives in the accessible name, the icon must be easy to recognize, and an ambiguous action uses a button with text.
keyboard: Keyboard focus on the element opens the balloon at once.
Enter and Space run the action of the element and neither open nor close the balloon.
Esc closes the balloon and does not reach the page; the focus stays on the element. With the balloon closed, Esc is not intercepted.
accessibility.focus: The balloon never takes focus: focus stays on the element that opened it, with the focus drawing of that element. The balloon stays open while the pointer is over it (WCAG 1.4.13).
accessibility.contrast: The text uses color/tooltip-foreground on color/tooltip: 6.69 to 1 in light and 7.47 to 1 in dark, above 4.5 to 1.
accessibility.color_alternative: The explanation is conveyed by the text; color is not the only signal.

invalid_combinations: No for, or a for that matches no element in the same root: the balloon is not drawn.
A side that is not top, bottom, left or right: the balloon is not drawn.
A for that points at a disabled element or at an element that does not receive focus: the balloon is not drawn.
A relation that is not description or name: the balloon is not drawn and no reference is written.
relation name with empty text: the element is left without a name.
Adding a title, icon, action, link, arrow or border: the scope is text only.
Moving focus to the balloon: focus stays on the element.
Using nph-tooltip for content with action or focus: use nph-popover.
Relying on the balloon on touch: it never opens there.
An icon-only button with aria-label equal to the balloon text and the default relation: the text is read twice; use relation name.
anti_patterns: Using the balloon as helper text or a field error message.
Putting in the balloon information without which the element cannot be used.
Cutting, truncating or breaking a word to fit in the balloon.
Opening the balloon from code on a timer or on a click.
An ambiguous action as an icon-only button: on touch it has no visible name.
Applying elevation/dropdown in a subtree with a data-nph-color-scheme different from the root: the shadow may use the color of the root scheme.
